column2: Praised thus, the great goddess Narmada, best of rivers, became manifest to the brahmins, Yudhishthira.
Narmada said: "I am pleased and grant boons, brahmins; I will give you the fruit you desire." Then great clouds rained, and grain became abundant,
and bulbs, roots, fruits, vegetables and ease came to all who took refuge there. Markandeya said: Those who recite this hymn, lord of men, or hear it with supreme devotion, taking refuge,
to them at the time of death this best of rivers gives a wholly pure goal. Rising at dawn, one should thus glorify Rudra, Uma and the goddess;
all sins dissolve, and the great-souled take refuge; freed from sins they rejoice in heaven — by Shambhu's word, and not otherwise.
Markandeya said: Those persons were seen, none other, resorting to the bank of the Narmada, engaged in bathing and worship of the gods — five of great strength.
They were seen by all the brahmins versed in the Vedas and Vedangas. The brahmins said: "At day's end a pair of women was seen, fierce and terrifying,
and three old men with nooses in their hands, terrifying, hard to withstand, hard to look upon, restless, moving here and there;
they speak with fearful voices, longing to be seen; all of them, estranged from one another, look at one another."
What was said in those groups I shall tell you in full. The persons said: "We all bathed at the holy places in the east, west, south
and north with devotion, yet that sin was not removed; here we have become sinless by the power of this holy place.
Hear, all you sages, brahmins like flames of fire, of dreadful sins of embodied beings that are beyond thought:
by this most sinful one the guru's wife was defiled; by another a friend's gold was stolen;
a fierce killing of a brahmin was done, and another sin was committed by another; liquor was drunk by this one, though unintentionally;
the sin of killing a cow was done by this one sinner. All these sins, lord of men, were committed even unintentionally."
The brahmins, seeing those most sinful ones rid of their impurity by the power of this holy place and the power of the Narmada,
reflected: "No sins can ever enter here." Reflecting thus, all those most sinful ones together
quickly rose up, meditating on Hari in their hearts, bathed in the holy water of the Reva and satisfied the ancestors and gods,
bowed to the god Bhaskara, meditated on Janardana in their hearts, and circumambulated with devotion the blazing fire;
the sinners, distressed by their sins, fell into it, best of the Pandavas; forming a sattvic wish, they gave up their lives and went to heaven.
Sinless, they were then seen by the fortunate brahmins on the northern bank of the Narmada standing in aerial cars, Yudhishthira.
An incomparable wonder was seen by the sages on the bank of the Narmada. From that time on all those brahmins, free of attachment and hatred,
joyfully serve Ravitirtha out of desire for liberation.
I shall tell it briefly, having seen its inner nature too: as Kurukshetra is purifying, so Ravitirtha is heard to be.
It was told long ago by the Lord to Shanmukha, Yudhishthira, and heard by all of Rudra's ganas; I was near him there.

Those who go there at an eclipse of the sun, six-faced one — at Ravitirtha the fruit is equal to Kurukshetra.
skandapuran:94:5	In bathing, giving, japa and especially oblation, the merit is the same as at Kurukshetra; there is no need for deliberation.
Whether in a village or in the forest, the Narmada is holy everywhere, lord of the earth, but especially at Ravitirtha on the sun's festival.
Those with senses controlled who go there with devotion on a Sunday, at vyatipata and vaidhriti, at a transit or an eclipse,
freed from desire and anger and likewise from attachment and hatred, with Vaishnava story and Vedic study, son of Pritha —
by reciting a single verse of the Rig Veda, Yajur Veda, Sama Veda or Atharvan they obtain the whole fruit;
by the Gayatri a man obtains the fruit of the four Vedas. At dawn one should worship the god with gifts of food and gold.
Whoever bathes there and gives a tawny cow to a worthy brahmin has given the earth with its mountains, woods and forests;
Bhurloka, Bhuvarloka, Maharloka and Janaloka, Tapoloka and Satyaloka, and the twenty-one netherworlds —
all these are given by him who has given a cow; the sin they committed over a year perishes, no doubt.
Yudhishthira said: "How is the goal holy, dear one? Tell me this truly." Markandeya said: Long ago at the beginning of the Krita age, Brahma, Grandsire of the world,
produced the whole fourfold host of beings, and by it the earth became crowded, delight of Pandu.
Then afterwards he reflected: "How will the world fare? How will devoted men go to heaven?
And how will the sun become greatly pleased with the worlds?" As Viranchi pondered, there rose from the fire-pit
one blazing, full of radiance, with a swinging bell ringing. Seeing that most fortunate tawny cow in the midst of the pit,
Brahma, guru of the world, bowed to her and said this: "Salutation to you, holy Kapila, unsurpassed in all the worlds,
auspicious one, goddess of blessings, saluted in the three worlds; you are Lakshmi, you are steadfastness and intelligence, the pure one, fair-faced lady;
you are renowned as the goddess Uma, you are Shachi, no doubt; you are Vaishnavi, great goddess, you are Brahmani, fair-faced one;
you are Kumari, fortunate one, and devotion and faith likewise; the night of doom for beings, Kumari, the supreme sovereign.
You are the truti and the ghati, the muhurta and the moment; the year, seasons and months; you are ever Time and the Person.
There is nothing without you in the three worlds with the moving and unmoving." Praised thus by the supreme lord, the tawny cow,
the most fortunate one, delighted, said to the supreme lord: "I am pleased with your words, god of gods, guru of the world."
Brahma said: "You were produced by me for the good of the world, supreme sovereign; go from heaven to the mortal world, desiring the welfare of the worlds.
Those who give you according to rule — you who contain all gods and all worlds — shall dwell in heaven."
Thus addressed by the supreme lord, the holy tawny cow came to the surface of the earth, saluted by the best of gods,
and by her the earth became purified, delight of Pandu. Hear from me the gods who dwell in her limbs:
the god Agni is in her mouth and the serpents in her teeth; Dhatri and Vidhatri are her lips, and the Ashvins are in her ears;
the wielder of the thunderbolt is in her horn, the Grandsire between her horns; Kala is in the middle, dear one, and likewise Varuna the noose-bearer;
the blessed god Yama is above her mouth; the metres are in her navel, the gods in her thighs, O Bharata;
the earth is in her navel, the mountains in her joints; trees, bushes and creepers are ranged along the paths of her joints;
the sages are in the pores of her hair, delight of Pandu; all the ancestors are in her sinews; her urine is born of all holy places;
and her dung is best of all, purifying and destroying sin; all the serpents are in her hooves, the sun's rays in the tip of her tail.
Thus the tawny cow contains all gods; those who meditate on her at home with devotion are freed, no doubt.
Whoever, rising at dawn, circumambulates her daily with devotion has circumambulated the earth with its seven continents.
Whoever bathes Shankara with the five products of a tawny cow, or Vishnu, support of the world, or the Sun or another deity —
bathing with the five nectars and with cow's products with devotion, son of Pandu — or who daily for a year gives a tawny cow to a learned brahmin,
this fruit is declared equal by Shankara, Yudhishthira. Whoever, well restrained, gives to a brahmin at Ravitirtha
a tawny, black, white, red or pink cow, giving milk, young, fair, with her calf and furnished with cloth,
with gilded horns and silver hooves, thinking of the brahmin as Vishnu, of himself as Vishnu and of the cow as the Sun —
whoever gives thus, mighty-armed one, has his dwelling in heaven; he is freed from the killing of a brahmin, from the dreadful drinking of liquor,
from going to the guru's wife, theft, betrayal of one's master, killing cows, betraying a friend's trust, and the sin of reviling the guru,
from ruin of the family's standing and lineage, from stepping over offerings to the god, from going to a maiden, from eating what is forbidden,
from the dreadful going to a shudra woman and going to the deformed, from arson, poisoning and false witness —
all that sin the gift of a cow destroys, son of Pandu. At the holy Surabhi confluence, spat upon, destroying sin,
whoever with devotion has shraddha performed for a departed one, son of Kunti, with him the Sun is pleased, and Bhava is well pleased.
Whatever gift is given there with devotion for the Sun, one goes happily to the world of Mitra by the grace of the Narmada.
At Dadhichchhanda, Madhuchchhanda, Devayana the giver of happiness and Bhimeshvara, best of the Kurus, equal merit is praised.
On the earth bounded by the ocean these five holy places are famous; those dwelling on earth who do not know them are as good as dead, no doubt.
Bathing, worship of the gods, japa, oblation, honouring brahmins, the gift of land, clothing and food with devotion,
sandals, umbrellas and beds, the gift of a house, son of Pandu, the gift of a village or a maiden, the gift of elephants and horses,
the gift of learning and carts — the one who gives fearlessness to all goes to all the holy places in going to Ravitirtha, Yudhishthira.
By the power of pilgrimage diseases are destroyed; enemies become friends, and poison becomes like nectar;
all the planets become pleased, and Divakara is pleased with him. The merit that arises for men from drinking the water of this holy place
equals a year's service of the ashvattha and the gift of a tawny cow; I shall tell you that fruit, lord of the earth, out of devotion.
All sins dissolve like water in a broken vessel for those who set out toward the holy place, no doubt.
Here the outer and inner holy place has been told to you, lord of the earth. From the most sinful, the ungrateful, those hostile to master and friend,
this auspicious account of the holy place should always be kept hidden by the wise.
All the gods who stayed there installed the husband of Uma; Indra, Chandra, Yama and the Sun installed him for the accomplishment of their desires,
and all the gods, delighted and thriving, went to their places in the sky. Because the skulls of the danavas fell there, fortunate one,
from that time that holy place has been called Karoti, lord of the earth, renowned in the land of Bharata on the surface of the earth, delight of Pandu.
On the eighth and fourteenth of the bright fortnight, fasting with devotion before the trident-bearer, one should keep vigil at night,
with talk of his stories and Vedic chanting; when clear dawn comes, having carefully worshipped Sthanu,
bathing him with the five nectars one should worship him with sandal, and worship him carefully with flowers of a hundred petals;
reciting the Bahurupa mantra and giving a fee, one obtains the fruit of Adityeshvara on the Narmada.
Whoever recites the power of the holy place he has heard, lord of men — I shall tell you all of it with devotion, lord of the earth.
Standing navel-deep in the water according to the rule stated, with senses controlled, one should have shraddha performed there for the departed,
with various foremost recitations by those devoted to Vedic study; having honoured the brahmin with cows and gold, with clothing, betel and food,
with ornaments and gifts of silk, son of Pandu, having honoured him at that holy place, one should give food as he desires;
it becomes a crore-fold for him; there is no need for deliberation. Whoever with devotion gives up his body at that holy place, giver of honour,
hear, lord of men, the merit that is his at the holy place: as long as a man's bones remain in the water of the Narmada,
so long does the righteous one dwell in the most rare world of Shiva; then, falling from there in time, the god enters human birth
and is born a glorious lord of a crore of banners, no doubt, endowed with every dharma, intelligent, with living sons,
famous on the face of the earth and long-lived. By Indra, Chandra, Yama, the Rudras, the Adityas and the Vasus,
and by all the Vishvedevas, the lord of the thirty gods was installed on the northern bank of the Narmada, desiring the good of the worlds.
Whoever has a temple built there for the sake of a departed one — that best of men attains a good goal.
Whoever performs shraddha here with wealth earned justly — brahmins, kshatriyas, vaishyas, women and shudras honoured there —
they too go to the supreme world of Shankara, worshipped by the gods. The man who hears with devotion the greatness born of the holy place, O king,
his sin committed over six months perishes. Markandeya said: Then, king of kings, one should go to the excellent Kumareshvara,
famous among all holy places, and the excellent Agastyeshvara. Shanmukha practised austerity there, destroying all sins;
by bathing with supreme devotion perfection was attained, lord of men; the leader of the army of the gods, O king, crusher of all enemies,
became of fierce radiance and great-souled by serving the holy place. From that time that holy place has been famed on the bank of the Narmada.
Whoever at that holy place, with devotion, single-minded and with senses controlled, on the eighth and fourteenth, especially of Kartika,
bathes the lord of Girija with curd, milk and ghee — singing should be done there and pinda offerings according to rule,
with learned brahmins ever devoted to the six duties, son of Pritha; whatever is given there is imperishable, delight of Pandu.
It is a holy place beyond all holy places, made by the Moon, O king. This I have told you in full, the fruit born of Kumareshvara;
by seeing Kumara merit is obtained, delight of Pandu, and dying there one attains heaven — this truth was spoken by the Lord.
Then, king of kings, one should go to the excellent Agastyeshvara, where the fortunate Agastya, bull among sages, attained perfection.
Yudhishthira said: How did the fortunate Agastya, bull among sages, attain perfection — the pot-born, fortunate one, born of Mitra and Varuna,
resorting to the bank of the Narmada? Tell me all that. Markandeya said: It is a great question, great king, that you have asked;
I shall tell it to you; listen always with one mind. Long ago in the Krita age, dear one, the earth was afflicted by her burden,
and wishing to plead with the lord of the gods she went to the vault of heaven, O king, and told Indra that the world was oppressed by the burden of the daityas.
Indra said: "Brahma is the maker of the world, both yours and mine, lovely one; I shall go to Brahma's world with the ministers and gods."
Then they all went to where the lotus-seated one was. Brihaspati said: "Brahman, the earth has lost her support through the burden of the daityas;
unable to bear that burden, the goddess is going down to Rasatala. Devise a remedy for the earth, lord of the world;
creation rests in you for the benefit of all beings, lord of the world." The Grandsire said: "I am the maker of all worlds; the one born, not of a womb, but from a pot —
Agastya, a mass of austerity — is able to hold back the daityas. On one side stand the strength and radiance of all the gods,
and on the other side those of the chief of sages; there is no doubt of this." Hearing Brahma's words, all the gods with Vasava
then told another cause, O Bharata: "It is known, lord of the god of gods, what Vishvamitra intends to do.
This sacrifice has been performed by Vishvamitra for the sake of Trishanku, and out of rivalry with Vasishtha he created the parts of the sacrifice;
out of rivalry, creating a sky, he created another earth. As the Himalaya mountain stands on the earth
extending to the eastern and western oceans, accomplishing the work of the gods, so this Vindhya rivals it, through rivalry and through Kaushika.
The works of the gods are halted by Kaushika, lord of the gods; think of a remedy for these two matters, guru of your world."
Brahma said: "His only guru is the brahmin Agastya, bull among sages, unassailable to Kaushika, who is going astray.
Agastya will be the one to break the path, no doubt; the guru is the ruler of the self-controlled, of all, no doubt.
The growth of this mountain, the setting going of the path of the gods, and the restraint of the brahmin Kaushika all over the earth —
the son of Mitra and Varuna is capable of all these tasks." Having decided thus, the gods with Indra and the Grandsire
went with the earth to the Himalaya, king of mountains; they saw the brahmin yogi there in meditation,
firm and unmoving in meditation, a guide on the path of liberation. Seeing him, they began to praise him, with Indra, Chandra and Varuna.
The gods said: "Desire victory for the gods, blessed pot-born one; be gracious and kindly — fear has come upon the gods."
Agastya said: "What business has arisen that you have come so far to me, who always dwell in solitude, O gods?
Tell me what is to be done by me, and I will do it all." Then with his thousand eyes, lovely as a lotus pond stirred by a gentle breeze,
the slayer of Vritra urged on his guru. The lord of speech said: "Long ago, fortunate one, for the accomplishment of the gods' work,
all the oceans were drained by you, as by the Lord the world. All the thirty gods were routed by danavas proud of their strength;
all those gods were defeated and turned their backs on the danavas; to take away their boon the oceans were dried up long ago.
Now the earth is in distress — see her, the bearer of beings; afflicted by the burden of the daityas, the earth has gone down to Rasatala.
You must go to the southern quarter, mass of austerity, best of the twice-born; make the holy boundary of the Narmada and the ocean, great brahmin;
and the growth of the Vindhya mountain too — rescue the work of the gods. And Kaushika, your junior, is the one who sets going the wrong path."
Agastya said: "I shall do the gods' work; rest at ease, Earth. I go to the southern quarter, able to restrain my disciple;
I shall stop the growth of this mountain, no doubt." The gods said: "Having gone south, you are to be seen together with the gods, no doubt;
when the sun is in Leo, brahmin, those who go out of devotion to see you — their wealth and grain perish, and their happiness too, no doubt.
He will be seen for the sake of the gods' authority." Having promised this, the gods went with the earth.
Agastya, the mass of austerity, set out, and all around, from Agastya's stride, the earth shook.
With the speed of mind he reached where the ascetic Kaushika was. Kaushika, seeing his guru, prostrated with eight limbs:
I am blessed, tiger among sages, I am delighted by the sight of you. Taking a vessel of guest-water with curd and unbroken rice,
durva grass and sandal placed in the vessel with reverent devotion, having sprinkled his guru's feet, he spoke sweetly:
Give me your command, dear one; I am your servant, best of the twice-born. Agastya said: "Kaushika, give up obstructing the work of the gods;
do not proceed with work abandoned by the gods. If your devotion to me is firm, Vishvamitra,
then abandon all this setting going of the wrong path." Vishvamitra said: "The guru is the ruler of the self-controlled, the king the ruler of the wicked,
and here Yama, son of Vivasvat, is the ruler of those with hidden sins. Out of rivalry with Vasishtha, Trishanku's request was granted by me;
from today all that is abandoned, best of the twice-born." Thus answered, he went quickly to the most rare bank of the Reva,
reached the northern bank and began austerity there — the Narmada is holy in the three worlds and destroys sin.
Having made a supreme resolve, the son of Mitra and Varuna sat on a flat rock and practised vast austerity,
the pot-born one of great austerity living on air at all times; the excellent one was recognized as full of devotion by the Lord, Yudhishthira.
In the twelfth year the husband of Parvati became manifest and came to him. The Lord said: "Well done, well done, best of sages; the sky is illumined by your austerity.
I am truly pleased with you, son of Mitra and Varuna; even after ten million years I do not grant boons to others."
Agastya said: "Beyond the puddle of worldly existence, free of creation and birth, hard to perceive for the hosts of asuras, lord of the Pramathas, salutation to you.
Nandi, Skanda, the ganas and the gods toil in vain, deluded; the sages of praised vows headed by Sanatkumara
do not know your form, Shambhu, lord — salutation to you. Brahma and all the gods meditate on you day and night,
yet they do not see your form, creator god — salutation to you." The Lord said: "I am pleased with you, chief of brahmins, of upward seed, not born of a womb;
I am captured by your devotion and pleased, together with Uma." Agastya said: "If you are pleased, lord of gods, if a boon is to be given me,
be manifest at this holy place, if you truly are a giver of boons; always within the water, Maheshvara, overseer of dharma,
dwell ever in the rock on the northern bank of the Narmada; by your grace, lord of the world, I shall accomplish the gods' work."
Saying "So be it," the bull-borne lord of mountains went to Mount Kailasa. The one not born of a womb, endowed with the power of yoga, by knowledge and by the power of Shiva's linga,
went to the southern quarter, praised by hosts of gods, to an ascetic grove holy as could be, served by gods and danavas.
The tiger among sages entered the pure Devakambala; the goddess Sushama became steady, and so did the earth.
The gods rained down flowers with cries of victory again and again. Yudhishthira said: "Tell me the merit of that holy place, sage of good vows,
at its beginning, middle and end, with brahmins and kin, beneficial to the ancestors, to all holy places and to all beings."
Markandeya said: It is declared to give release to the ancestors at all times, lord of people. On the fourteenth of the dark fortnight in the month of Kartika, called Shiva's night,
the man who fasts with devotion, free of desire and anger, should take his place by a shami tree and keep vigil at night,
engaged in talk of his stories, with brahmins and accounts of dharma; and at night he should bathe the lord of gods with cow's ghee,
with a pot, half a pot or half of that, according to his means; he should light a lamp with ghee and have ghee given to a brahmin;
he should bathe the supreme Lord with the five nectars and cow's products. At dawn he should honour brahmins who are ever devoted to their own wives,
given to the study of the Veda and avoiding others' wives. People ever devoted to serving shudras, engaged in cheating,
fallen through false witness, ever intent on receiving gifts, given to hating the Veda, hunchbacked and always defective,
brahmins with missing or extra limbs — these are excluded at shraddha; those whose limbs are pure as the Veda prescribes are always to be honoured, Yudhishthira.
With the gift of land and clothing, and especially the gift of maidens, at times of shraddha and on auspicious conjunctions, they should be supported by the devout.
The gift of a cow should be made there for one's own good: with her calf, giving milk, fair, well fed and good-natured,
and with supreme devotion a blanket, wooden sandals and shoes, a quilt with gold and ornaments, betel and food;
the cow rich with the splendour of a bell and ornaments, covered with a pair of cloths, with gilded horns and silver hooves, with a bronze milking pail —
uttering the formula with supreme devotion, until the deluge — everything becomes a crore-fold, son of Pritha, whether good or bad.
Whoever with devotion recites or hears the account of the holy place is freed from all sins and dwells in Shiva's world.
I shall tell of that holy place which destroys the sin of the Sun. Yudhishthira said: "Joy arose for Rudra, best of the twice-born —
tell me briefly, fortunate one, best of sages." Markandeya said: I shall tell of the excellent Anandeshvara, best of kings.
Having slain the danavas, Shankara, god of gods, was worshipped by all the gods, kinnaras, yakshas and serpents;
attaining supreme joy, the bull-borne god danced, taking the form of Bhairava, with Gauri as half his body,
Bhairava surrounded by bhutas, vetalas, skeletons and bhairavas, on the northern and southern bank of the Narmada, delight of Pandu.
The lotus-seated one was installed there by the delighted hosts of Maruts; from that time the god has been called Anandeshvara.
On the eighth, the fourteenth and the full moon, lord of men, one should bathe according to rule, worship the god and anoint him with fragrant paste;
one should honour brahmins there according to one's means, Yudhishthira; the gift of a cow should be made there and likewise the gift of clothing.
On the thirteenth in spring one should have shraddha performed right there, with ingudi, jujubes, bilva, unbroken rice or water;
one should have shraddha performed for the departed at Anandeshvaratirtha; the departed will rejoice until the deluge.
Offspring, wealth and happiness come for seven births, and they have joy in birth after birth, Yudhishthira.
Markandeya said: Then, king of kings, one should go to the unsurpassed Matritirtha, near the confluence on the southern bank of the Narmada.
There the Mothers arose, king of kings, on the bank of the Narmada; there, entreated by Uma, the one with a serpent as sacred thread
said to the host of yoginis: "Alas, alas, this is not fitting." He said: "I am the giver of boons, granting boons to the host of yoginis."
The yoginis said: "May we be invincible to all the gods by your grace, Maheshvara, and famous on earth in the reckoning of holy places."
So be it, yoginis, he said, and vanished right there.
Markandeya said: Whoever at that holy place, with senses controlled, fasts on the ninth and with supreme devotion worships the circle of the Mothers,
with him the Mothers are pleased and the bull-borne god is pleased. For a barren woman, one whose children die, or one without sons, Yudhishthira,
a ritual bath should be begun there by excellent brahmins who know the mantras, with a pot containing gold, the five gems and fruits;
the woman who desires a son should be bathed from a bronze vessel with mantras; she obtains sons, vigorous and virtuous.
Whatever desire she meditates on, she obtains it, O king; there is no other holy place beyond Matritirtha, delight of Pandu.
Right after it, dear one, is the supreme Jalamadhyeshvara, renowned as Lingeshvara, saluted by gods and asuras.
Yudhishthira said: "The Reva that is never abandoned — how was she abandoned by Shambhu? Why should the trident-handed bearer of Pinaka stand in the midst of the water?
I wish to hear that from your mouth, best of the twice-born." Markandeya said: The installation is a wonder in this world, delight of Pandu;
wise through old age, I shall tell it, best of kings. In the beginning, in the Krita age, dear one, a danava proud of his strength,
called Kalabashpa, invincible to gods and danavas, practised vast austerity in the lovely water of the Narmada,
worshipping Mahadeva intensely with fierce austerity. Then the blessed Maheshvara with his consort was pleased.
The Lord said: "O child, name a boon; I am pleased with your devotion." Hearing the god's words, Kalabashpa said:

The gods have been routed by me through your grace, trident-bearer, but I was dismayed in battle; therefore I have worshipped you.
skandapuran:96:31	On whosoever's head I place my hand, Maheshvara, let that man not live in the world — grant me this boon.
The Lord said: "What you desire, daitya, shall be just so." Hearing these words, the daitya rushed at Shambhu himself:
I shall place my hand on your head — let me see if your word is not true. Rudra fled from him and went to Keshava for refuge;
having told Keshava everything, he hid right there within him. Keshava said: "I shall slay that wicked lord of the daityas, Mahadeva;
I shall make him place his hand on his own head, Maheshvara." Then, hastening, he entered the bank of the Narmada;
Krishna, wearing the guise of a woman, came before the daitya, endowed with the thirty-two marks, armed with Love's arrows.
In the spring, meditating on Shambhu everywhere, the woman who was Keshava, of fine conduct, wandered all through the forest to a banyan tree,
and she sported as if agitating minds, son of Dharma. And the danava Kalabashpa, most wicked, prowling,
entered the lovely forest where the fair-eyed one was: "I shall be your husband, invincible to gods and danavas,
and you shall be mistress of the three worlds; be gracious to me, lovely one." Shri Krishna said: "If you consider me your wife, let me have proof."
The danava said: "I myself shall be it, slender one; my oath is my means; I will do that — this I say in truth."
The woman said: "Do it, fortunate one; let your hand be placed on your head." Markandeya said: Blinded by desire, king of kings, he placed his hand on his head,
and at that instant he became ashes, like a heap of grass burned up. Then a rain of flowers fell upon Keshava;
all the gods, their fever gone, went to heaven, each to his place; and when Kalabashpa had been struck down, Vishnu went to the Ocean of Milk.
Whoever hears with devotion this story of the danava, and whoever performs shraddha right there, free of desire and anger,
by him all his forefathers are raised from hell. Whoever at that field gives to a brahmin versed in the Veda,
the whole fruit of his gift surpasses that of Kurukshetra. Whoever touches this linga made by Shankara —
by mere touch that man becomes a dweller with Rudra. For this reason, O king, the world-guardians and gods,
the goddess Durga, the four-armed slayer of Madhu, the danavas and all the rest, for the protection of the Lord,
guard it at all times in the guise of household affairs, becoming like sons and brothers, bearing the form of relations to a master.
Lingeshvara, king of kings, is guarded by the gods even today.
The serpents said: "Just as you are the mother of all serpents on earth, so she too is especially not to be deceived, being like a mother."
Then, angered by those words, she became like the fire of doom: "Whatever serpents on earth do not carry out my word,
all of them, thoughtless ones, shall go into the mouth of the bearer of oblations." Frightened by those words, those who wrapped themselves around the horse's hairs...
some vanished into the divine quarters, filled with fear of Kadru's curse; some vanished into the water of the Ganga, some into the Sarasvati;
some were carried to the great ocean, some entered the caves of the Vindhya; Maninaga, best of serpents, taking refuge in the water of the Narmada, O king,
practised vast devotion on the northern bank of the Narmada. Bearing his mother's curse, the naga entered the water of the Narmada:
By your grace, lord, may I cross over my mother's curse, so that I do not go into the mouth of the bearer of oblations, lord of the world.
The Lord said: "By my command, child, you will not go into the mouth of the bearer of oblations; you will even dwell in my world, son."
Maninaga said: "Stay in this place, Mahadeva, by a portion of yourself; stay in the water of the Narmada by a thousandth part,
for the benefit of the worlds and under my name, Shankara." The Lord said: "Install a supreme linga of your own by my command, serpent."
Having said this, the god vanished then with Shiva. Those who at that holy place, pure and with restrained minds,
on the fifth, fourteenth and eighth of the bright fortnight always worship him with devotion, son of Pritha, do not come near Yama.
People bathe the odd-eyed one who bears Uma as half his body with curd, honey, ghee and milk;
those who with devotion bathe the god who burned Kama's body, the slayer of great asuras, see the supreme state.
Those devoted to the six duties, dear one, and avoiding intimacy with shudras also go to the supreme world, free of all sins.
No one should honour vratyas, the unruly, eunuchs, usurers, cultivators and brahmins who sow discord.
The one in whose house is a shudra woman, the one who drives a buffalo — such brahmins are to be kept far away at vows and shraddha, lord of kings.
The one-eyed, the kunda and golaka and physicians are excluded; these brahmins are not to be honoured, son of Pritha, at the auspicious Maninageshvara.
If one desires the upward journey of the ancestors and oneself, brahmins with lovely and whole limbs are always to be honoured.
He goes to the supreme world until the deluge; then, falling from heaven, he is born in a great family.
Whoever sees the god Maninageshvara, lord of men, and with good devotion gives a cow, a bed, an umbrella, a maiden and a maidservant
to a worthy recipient, king of kings, if he desires his own good — and he should have fragrant flowers, perfumes and garments given;
men who with devotion give a lamp, grain and a fine house with all its furnishings go to heaven.
At Maninaga, O king, whoever gives a golden serpent —
his sins dissolve like water in an unbaked pot. Food prepared with Narmada water given to a brahmin —
they too are freed from sins and sport with the gods. Those who are generous yet enjoy pleasures, ever delighting in accounts of dharma,
devoted to gods, brahmins and gurus, intent on serving holy places, devoted to mother, father and master, free of anger and malice —
men endowed with all these virtues, delight of Pandu, are born desiring heaven, and their dwelling will be in heaven.
Maninaga is the best of all holy places, best of kings. Whoever recites or hears this holy account of the holy place
is freed from sin and honoured in Shiva's world. Poison does not overcome them, and they roam as they please.
Whoever bathes on the sixth of Bhadrapada and on the new moon of Bhadra — the attainment of that fruit of merit comes by telling this account.
Maheshvara said: "I am pleased, goddess, mother of the world, Kapila, supreme sovereign; why have you worshipped me? Tell me, fair-faced goddess."
Surabhi said: "I was created by the supreme lord for the benefit of the worlds; every work in the world is accomplished by my grace.
Let all the worlds see the trident-bearer by your grace; be present at this holy place, Shambhu, desiring the good of the worlds."
Markandeya said: From that time the holy place has been famous on earth; by a single bath, king of kings, it removes all sin.
Whoever with devotion has a cow given at Gopalesha — a worthy cow with gold should be given to a worthy excellent brahmin,
with cloth, young, fair, giving milk and with a bull — on the fourteenth or the eighth of the dark fortnight, Yudhishthira,
in all months and especially in Kartika, he should have her given with supreme devotion to a brahmin devoted to Vedic study.
Those who give according to rule and those who receive according to rule — both do holy deeds, and even the onlookers share in the merit.
Pinda offerings should be made for the departed by those full of feeling; by a single pinda, king of kings, the departed go to the supreme goal.
Those who bow to Rudra with devotion day after day, their sin dissolves like water in a broken vessel.
Whoever releases a bull at that holy place, O king — Yudhishthira said: "The fruit that comes to men from releasing a bull, dear one,
tell me all of it now with care, best of the twice-born." Markandeya said: The fruit from a bull endowed with all auspicious marks,
I shall tell you; listen, son of Dharma. In Kartika and Vaishakha, on the full moon, lord of men,
being in Rudra's presence, pure, bathed and with senses controlled, one should perform the release of the bull, O king, to please Hara.
Standing in a pure place one should release four auspicious heifers for the bull, endowed with all good marks:
May Mahadeva be pleased, and Brahma, Vishnu and the others. As many as are the hairs on all the limbs of the bull, lord of men,
for so many years is one honoured in Shiva's world; having dwelt in Shiva's world, one is afterwards born among mortals,
born in a great family abounding in wealth and grain, handsome among the handsome, among those rich in learning and truthful.
I have told you of holy Gopaleshvara, Yudhishthira, the linga that came forth from the cow's body on the southern bank of the Narmada.
Go with supreme devotion to where the god, the guru of the world, is, for the destruction of sins and the attainment of a dwelling in heaven, O king.
The linga increases happiness, grants victory and destroys sorrow; by a single pinda offering one raises three generations.
Whatever is given with devotion, whether little or much, all of it becomes a hundred thousandfold, by the command of Gautama too.
It is the supreme holy place among holy places, declared by Rudra himself. Markandeya said: On the southern bank of the Narmada is a supremely lovely holy place,
Shankhachudeshvara, famous across the earth; Shankhachuda dwells there, delight of Pandu,
having settled on the bank of the Narmada out of fear of Vinata's son, son of Pritha. Whoever at that holy place, with devotion, pure and collected,
bathes Shankhachuda with honey, curd and ghee, keeps vigil at night before the god, lord of men,
honours brahmins of praised vows with curd and rice, and likewise gives a cow, destroys all sins.
Whoever at that holy place perishes even by snakebite, son of Pritha, also goes to the supreme world by the command of Shankhachuda.
Whoever bathes at that holy place, fasting and with senses controlled, reciting the one-syllabled mantra with upraised arms to the sun,
his sin earned since birth perishes at that very moment; sin earned in seven births is surely destroyed by the Gayatri.
With ten repetitions the Gayatri destroys sin born in this birth, with a hundred sin done before, with a thousand the sin of three births.
Whatever japa, Vedic or worldly, has been recited, lord of people, burns up sin at once as fire burns grass.
But if, relying on that very power, one ever commits sin, then for him, through his ignorance, there is never any fruit.
